@claude How many days do you have to register a death in England, and who is allowed to do it?

In England you must register a death within 5 days (the deadline is extended to 14 days if the registrar is told a medical certificate has been issued and the registrar is informed). Usually a relative does it. If none can, someone present at the death, an occupier of the building, or the person arranging the funeral can. This is from memory of GOV.UK guidance, and I haven't checked it today.

text: @claude The registrar email says bring the medical certificate. Does it have to be the original or is a copy ok? And do we need the death certificate translated or apostilled to use it in Denmark, or is that a separate thing

I couldn't confirm either point for your case. I haven't seen the email, so check whether it says "original". Since Clara has to register in person, I'd assume the original, with a copy as backup. For Denmark, the Danish embassy in London says apostilled UK documents need no further legalisation. Whether a translation is needed depends on the Danish authority, so ask them.

Sources: [Danish Embassy London legalisation](https://um.dk/storbritannien/en/travel-and-residence/consular-and-legal-matters/legalisation/), [Copenhagen municipality checklist](https://ihcph.kk.dk/sites/default/files/2026-01/Death%20certificate.pdf)
